title: Density is a manifest lever (airy / standard / tight) -- the plumbing
change: THE PROFILES CURRENTLY DIFFER ONLY BY TEXT COLOUR -- verified: visible=False appears 0 times and collapsed=True 0 times across all three manifests. Joe's ruling: the profiles must differ in HOW THE PANEL ORGANISES INFORMATION, on two axes only -- what is folded away, and how much air sits between what remains. This task builds the SECOND axis as plumbing ONLY; a later task makes the per-profile fold decisions. Pentagram logic governs: ONE systemic decision, not per-widget fiddling; no new components, no new colours, no new type. (1) SCHEMA: add an optional 'density' key to the manifest defaults, accepting exactly 'airy' | 'standard' | 'tight', defaulting to 'standard' when absent. Validate it in the same place and style the existing defaults are validated (manifests/__init__.py), so an invalid value raises ManifestError like any other schema breach. (2) VALUES: curious='airy', expert='standard', ml='tight'. (3) COMPOSITOR: in compose(), read the resolved density and set it as a Qt dynamic property on the PANEL ROOT (one setProperty + unpolish/polish, mirroring how _apply_spec already handles 'prominence'), so a single property drives the whole panel's rhythm. Do not add per-widget spacing specs and do not touch _apply_spec's existing behaviour. (4) QSS: add descendant rules keyed on that root property -- Qt stylesheets support descendant selectors, so rules take the shape #<PanelObjectName>[density="airy"] <Selector> {{ ... }}. Step ONLY spacing/padding/margin/line-height-equivalents, and step them off the EXISTING scale in tokens.py (SPACE_XS, SPACE_SM and siblings, GUTTER) -- airy takes one step up, tight takes one step down, and you must not invent a number, add a spacing token, or change any colour, size, weight, font, radius or border. Cover at minimum the chat reply rhythm (Joe: 'when Curious replies the responses should have more space vertically in their answers'), inter-region gaps, and control padding. (5) THE PIN IS ABSOLUTE: density='standard' must resolve to EXACTLY the spacing the panel renders today -- expert is pinned to v5.42.0 by L5-5. Achieve that by writing NO rule for the standard case at all; standard is the unstyled baseline, and airy/tight are the only rules that exist. A diff that adds or edits any unconditional spacing rule is a failure. (6) Add tests/test_rope_density.py: assert each manifest declares its expected density, assert an invalid density raises ManifestError, assert the generated stylesheet contains airy and tight rules that are not byte-identical, and assert NO rule is emitted for density='standard'. Record the derivation in docs/PROFILES.md under 'Derived design decisions' in the form 'X derived from Y because Z'.

title: Curious folds, ML surfaces economics, Expert untouched -- the composition decisions
change: THE FIRST AXIS: what each profile folds away. Manifests only -- do NOT touch the compositor, qss.py, synapse_panel.py, or expert.py. The compositor already supports 'visible' and 'collapsed' per widget and neither has ever been used; this task finally uses them. THE INVARIANT THAT GOVERNS EVERYTHING: identical agent capability in every profile. Folding changes what is SHOWN, never what the agent can DO -- no tool, gate, permission or command may be removed, and anything collapsed must remain reachable by the artist in one action. (1) CURIOUS -- reserved and progressive. Fold the readouts a first-session artist cannot yet act on: diagnostic/telemetry chrome and token/economic readouts become collapsed=True (present, one click away, not competing). Keep hero and fully visible the things that TEACH: the verb rail (EXPLAIN/FIX/OPTIMIZE/BUILD HDA -- it is the discovery mechanism), the command and palette hints, connect and corpus. The result must be a panel doing one thing at a time. (2) ML -- the economist's read. Everything expert shows stays shown; additionally promote the token/cost/model economics OUT of being tab-hidden into always-visible prominence, so the numbers are readable without a click. Add no widget that does not already exist in the widget registry. (3) EXPERT -- change NOTHING. expert.py must not appear in the diff. It is pinned to v5.42.0 by L5-5 and it is also, deliberately, the dense unguided baseline the other two are composed against; Expert reads as expert BY CONTRAST, not by gaining anything. (4) Use only widget ids that already exist in the compositor's registry -- an unknown id must fail resolve(), so verify each against known_widget_ids() rather than guessing a name. (5) Add tests/test_rope_profile_composition.py: assert curious collapses at least one widget and expert collapses none and hides none; assert ml leaves every widget expert shows visible; assert all three manifests still resolve() cleanly; and assert the widget-id SET available to the agent is identical across all three profiles (capability invariant -- composition may reorder, fold or re-emphasise, never remove). Record each decision in docs/PROFILES.md under 'Derived design decisions' in the form 'X derived from Y because Z', and update the three-profile table so its 'What the screen shows' column describes what the manifests now actually do.
